expectations.text: B1: Gives honest advice (CHIP-8 or LC-3 first, or a scoped GB plan) without dumping code
expectations.evidence: Honest scoped advice with tradeoffs and no code: 'Here's the honest tradeoff', 'Realistic effort: CHIP-8 is a weekend; a Game Boy that boots Tetris is several weekends', two paths offered ('1. Straight to Game Boy... 2. One-weekend bridge first — the LC-3 VM'), plus scoping questions ('Two questions to set scope'). FILES WRITTEN (0); no implementation code dumped, only links (Cinoop, 0dmg, LC-3 VM).

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Answer ends with 'Default if you have no preference: Rust with 0dmg, straight to the Game Boy, skipping the bridge.' No concrete command to run and no expected output/behaviour is given anywhere; 'load a ROM, print its header bytes, set PC to 0x0100' is a milestone description, not a runnable checkpoint command.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions a concrete GB difficulty such as the PPU timing, MBC banking, or CPU test ROMs (blargg)
expectations.evidence: Concrete difficulties named: 'validated against Blargg's `cpu_instrs` test ROM', 'Memory bank controllers (MBC1/MBC3) — cartridges swap 16 KB banks', 'A PPU with scanline timing — you render line-by-line against the LY register'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0), FILES WRITTEN (0); only read calls into '.agents/skills/build-your-own-x/skills/emulator-virtual-machine/...'. No install commands run or suggested.
